overview: Zambia is a landlocked country in southern Africa. Its capital and largest city is Lusaka. Zambia became independent from the United Kingdom in 1964. It is one of Africa's biggest producers of copper, and English is the official language.

geography.text: Most of Zambia is a high plateau covered by savanna and woodland. The Zambezi river forms its southern border with Zimbabwe, where it plunges over Victoria Falls, one of the largest waterfalls in the world. Lake Kariba, on the same river, is one of the largest artificial lakes in the world.

history.text: Bantu-speaking peoples settled the region, and kingdoms such as the Lozi grew up along the Zambezi. Cecil Rhodes's British South Africa Company took control in the 1890s, and the territory became Northern Rhodesia. Copper mining made it valuable. Zambia became independent in 1964 under Kenneth Kaunda.

events.title: Victoria Falls
events.text: David Livingstone reaches the falls and names them.

events.title: Company rule
events.text: The British South Africa Company takes control.

government.text: Zambia is a presidential republic with a history of peaceful elections. In 2021 opposition leader Hakainde Hichilema won the presidency, the third time power had passed to the opposition.

economy.text: Copper makes up most of Zambia's exports, and it is one of Africa's biggest producers. Cobalt, emeralds and farming are also important. Zambia defaulted on its debts in 2020 and has restructured them.

culture.text: Zambia shares Victoria Falls, 'the smoke that thunders', with Zimbabwe. Bats gather in their millions in Kasanka National Park each year in one of the largest mammal migrations on Earth.

items.title: Victoria Falls
items.text: One of the largest waterfalls in the world.

items.title: Kasanka bats
items.text: About 10 million fruit bats arrive each year.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport. In 2012 Zambia won the Africa Cup of Nations in Gabon, near where the national team died in a plane crash in 1993. The women's team played at its first World Cup in 2023.

items.title: Barbra Banda
items.text: Star forward of the women's team.
